text:
priya: Noticed a cluster of TLS verify failures for ap-south ingress starting ~09:12 UTC. Correlates with RBAC change to keystore access pinned to a service identity binding this morning.

priya: sample proxy error from edge-proxy-12:

priya: ```edge-proxy-12.log: 2026-03-23T09:14:21Z WARN tls verify failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (subject="CN=svc-ingress-proxy")```

kevin: Hmm. Did the cert issuance pipeline rotate keys earlier? Which principal did we grant access to in that RBAC change?

priya: Audit shows a conditional bind: 

priya: ```audit.log: 2026-03-23T09:10:45Z IAM Bind applied user=infra-deploy@redwood role=keystore.decrypt condition=expr:"request.auth.claims.aud == 'infra'"```

mike: That condition will block any request that doesn't carry aud claim == infra. Our cert-manager agent sometimes runs with token_aud=proxy when on node-level. Looks like cert-manager couldn't unwrap the private key, so proxies kept presenting older certs -> downstream rejects.

anya: Impact matrix: ingestion, embeddings-rank, and telemetry collectors saw increased 502s. Not full outage but degraded. SLOs impacted for 8-12% of requests in ap-south over 15m.

sam: Quick remediation options: 1) revert IAM bind (fast), 2) add secondary binding for proxy-aud, 3) patch cert-manager to set aud=infra. Which is least risky?

kevin: Revert is fastest. I can push a rollback to IAM in 3m. But we should gather KMS deny counts to ensure we didn't also hit quota/backoff issues.

audit-bot: KMS Deny spike detected: resource=projects/keystore/cryptoKeys/global-edge key=decrypt count=78 in 5m (threshold=10).

priya: Thanks. I'll roll a targeted cert reissue after revert. We should avoid mass reissues if not necessary.

mike: Rolling IAM revert now. Command: 

mike: ```gcloud iam roles bindings remove --role=roles/keystore.decrypt --member=serviceAccount:infra-deploy@redwood --condition='expr:request.auth.claims.aud=="infra"'```

ops-bot: IAM change submitted by mike at 09:18 UTC. Change-ID: iam-20260323-0920.

priya: Post-change: cert-manager rewrap job started on affected nodes (job=cm-rewrap-31805).

audit-bot: KMS Deny count returned to baseline (3 in last 5m).

anya: Handshake failure rate normalized within 6m of revert. Good recovery.

kevin: Follow-ups (short):
- Add CI test to simulate token aud variants + KMS decrypt success/fail.
- Ensure KMS audit payload includes full impersonation chain (subject, delegated_by).
- Run a config sweep to ensure all proxies use minVersion TLS1.3.

sam: Also propose a small automation: when KMS Deny for a role > 20/min and associated TLS handshake errors spike, run an alert and optionally auto-revert a recent IAM binding within a safe window (with human approve). I'll file a GH issue.

priya: Security note: tie this into our compliance checklist. Conditioned IAM bindings are powerful but brittle for cross-service impersonation flows. Include a test matrix in design docs.

mike: Filed follow-up ticket: https://internal.redwood/tickets/SEC-2026-048 (CI + runbook updates).

ops-bot: Incident incident-20260323-keystore-impersonation created (P3). Linked to ticket SEC-2026-048.

kevin: I'll own the CI test and the audit-logging change. Priya, can you own the proxy TLS minVersion sweep?

priya: Yup, will run a config job and report status in 24h. Closing thread once postmortem is up.
